claims.text: An anisotropic grain texture in Q235 steel produces heterogeneous grain-boundary electrochemical potentials.
Heterogeneous grain-boundary electrochemical potentials accelerate localized corrosion in chloride-rich environments.
A uniformly recrystallized microstructure with minimized texture anisotropy suppresses corrosion onset in Q235 steel.
Cold rolling induces anisotropic texture in Q235 steel.
A low-temperature stress-relief treatment minimizes residual-stress confounding while retaining the cold-rolled texture.
Full recrystallization annealing produces an isotropic grain structure in Q235 steel.
Differences in grain orientation and texture specifically generate grain-boundary character and surface-potential heterogeneities.
Potential heterogeneity in anisotropic cold-rolled microstructures promotes localized micro-galvanic corrosion.
Recrystallized samples have uniform grain orientations.
Uniform grain orientations produce a homogeneous electrochemical response.
A homogeneous electrochemical response suppresses localized corrosion.
Stress-relieved cold-rolled samples will exhibit faster and more localized corrosion than recrystallized samples under identical chloride exposure.
Stress-relieved cold-rolled samples will initiate pits earlier than recrystallized samples.
Recrystallized samples will exhibit a more uniform corrosion morphology than stress-relieved cold-rolled samples.
Recrystallized samples will show delayed pitting onset relative to stress-relieved cold-rolled samples.
Residual stress and other microstructural factors may continue to interact with texture after stress relief.

contradictions.description: The recrystallized condition is described as isotropic, but it is also said to have uniform grain orientations. An isotropic texture generally entails a broad or random orientation distribution, whereas uniform orientation would constitute strong preferred texture.
